mainTopic: Which images are forbidden under לא תעשון אתי, and why רבן גמליאל's moon pictures were allowed
overview: This amud asks why רבן גמליאל was allowed to have pictures of the moon. It first finishes a ברייתא about copying Temple objects: a seven-branched מנורה may not be made, even of other metals, though the חכמים reject רבי יוסי בר יהודה's claim that wood is also forbidden. The גמרא then tests the ban of לא תעשון אתי on picturing God's heavenly attendants. אביי limits it first to the four faces together, then to the attendants of the upper heaven. Along the way, the human face turns out to be forbidden from its own source, לא תעשון אותי. A ברייתא that clearly forbids making images of the sun and moon knocks out that approach. So the גמרא answers that others made רבן גמליאל's pictures for him, and it discusses the worry of suspicion with רב יהודה's ring and a בית כנסת in נהרדעא. It ends with three answers: a נשיא is never alone, the pictures were in pieces, or he made them in order to learn. A new משנה then begins about two witnesses who saw the moon in the morning in the east.

steps.title: A seven-branched מנורה may not be copied, even in other metals
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One may make a מנורה with five, six or eight branches, but not seven, even out of a metal other than gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may make a lamp of five, six or eight branches. But he may not make one of seven, even out of other kinds of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about Temple objects a person may not copy for himself. Here it is the מנורה's turn: seven branches are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five, six or eight branches are fine because they are not the real Temple shape. Seven is forbidden even in cheaper metal, because a מנורה made of other metals would still be valid in the בית המקדש. This ברייתא supports the idea that only an exact, usable copy is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The lamp with seven branches in the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה וְשֶׁל שִׁשָּׁה וְשֶׁל שְׁמוֹנָה.
phrases.english: [One may make a lamp] of five, of six, or of eight [branches].
But one of seven, he may not make,
even out of other kinds of metal.

steps.triggerLanguage: של חמשה ושל ששה ושל שמונה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא brought before this text to support the idea that only reproducible copies are forbidden.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the איסור of copying applies only to things that can be copied exactly.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about not copying the היכל and its vessels, here the מנורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the איסור follows the exact, valid form of the Temple object, not anything that just looks similar.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds that a wooden מנורה is also forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says that a seven-branched מנורה may not be made even of wood, because the חשמונאים made one of wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: one may not make it of wood either, the way the מלכי בית חשמונאי made it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds to the ברייתא. He forbids a wooden מנורה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is that the מלכי בית חשמונאי once made a מנורה out of wood. So in his view wood is also a valid Temple material, and copying it in wood is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
Also of wood one may not make it,
the way the kings of the Hasmonean dynasty made it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter opinion to the ברייתא's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seven-branched מנורה may not be made even of wood, based on what the חשמונאים did.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof from the חשמונאים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the חשמונאים' מנורה was not really wood. It was iron spits covered with tin, and it was later upgraded to silver and then to gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: is that your proof? They were iron spits covered with tin. When they became richer, they made them of silver. When they became richer again, they made them of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יוסי בר יהודה's proof. The חשמונאים never made a wooden מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof needed a wooden מנורה that was used in the בית המקדש. The חכמים say it was iron covered in tin, which is metal. So nothing shows that wood is valid, and a wooden copy stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (a way of brushing a proof aside)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the איסור covers only a seven-branched מנורה of metal, the kind valid in the בית המקדש. Wood is permitted.

phrases.english: They said to him: From there a proof?!
They were spits of iron,
and they covered them with tin.
phrases.notes: בעץ means tin, not wood (עץ). That small word is the whole point of the answer.

phrases.english: When they became rich, they made them of silver,
when they became rich again, they made them of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי בר יהודה's historical proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the חשמונאים is rejected, along with the added ban on wood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חשמונאים' מנורה was tin-covered iron, not wood.

steps.title: Challenge: images of heavenly attendants are forbidden even though they cannot be copied exactly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that things that cannot be copied exactly are permitted. A ברייתא forbids making images of God's attendants on high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really permitted to make images of attendants that cannot be copied exactly? But it was taught: 'You shall not make with Me' means you shall not make images of My attendants who serve before Me on high!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule that was just supported. Only exact, reproducible copies are forbidden, so heavenly beings (like the moon) should be allowed. A ברייתא seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from לא תעשון אתי that one may not image God's heavenly attendants. Those cannot be copied exactly, yet they are forbidden. That contradicts the idea behind רבן גמליאל's pictures of the moon.

phrases.english: And attendants whose likeness it is impossible to make,
is it permitted?
But it was taught: “You shall not make with Me”:
You shall not make the likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me on high!

steps.triggerLanguage: ושמשין שאי אפשר לעשות כמותן מי שרי והתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule supported by the ברייתא in steps 1-3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only reproducible things are forbidden to copy, which would permit images of the moon.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids images of heavenly attendants, which cannot be copied exactly, so non-reproducible things are also forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: only all four faces together are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the Torah forbade only an image showing the four faces together.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Torah forbade only the image of four faces together.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He narrows which heavenly attendants the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on attendants refers to the specific form with four faces together. The sun, moon and other heavenly things are not included, so רבן גמליאל's moon pictures stay permitted.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Torah forbade only
the image of four faces together.
phrases.notes: These are the four faces of the heavenly creatures that יחזקאל describes (יחזקאל 1).

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי לא אסרה תורה אלא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids images of any heavenly attendant, including the moon.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the four-faced image together is forbidden. Other images are permitted.

steps.title: Challenge: then why is a human face alone forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: If only all four faces together are forbidden, a human face alone should be permitted. Yet a ברייתא forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a human face alone should be permitted. Why then was it taught: all faces are permitted except the human face?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's answer. It uses a ברייתא that singles out the human face.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, one face alone (like the human face among the four) should be fine. But the ברייתא forbids the human face by itself, so it seems one face alone can be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (a way of showing that an idea goes too far)

phrases.english: But if so,
a human face alone should be permitted?
Why then was it taught:
All faces are permitted
except for the human face!

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא מעתה פרצוף אדם לחודיה תשתרי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that only the four faces together are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids a single human face, so not only the full four-faced image is forbidden.

steps.title: A separate source forbids the human face: 'Do not make Me'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב אידי reports from אביי's lecture that the human face is forbidden for a different reason. The פסוק can be read as לא תעשון אותי, 'do not make Me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב אידי said: I heard from אביי's lecture: 'You shall not make with Me' can be read as 'You shall not make Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a separate דרשה. The human face has its own reason for being forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אתי ('with Me') is read as אותי ('Me'). So the ban on a human face is not part of the four-faces rule. It is a separate איסור, and אביי's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Me (read in place of אִתִּי, 'with Me')

steps.whatToRemember: So far, אביי limits the ban on heavenly attendants to the four faces together. A human face is forbidden separately, from לא תעשון אותי. The next steps keep testing how far the ban on heavenly attendants reaches.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the human face is forbidden because it is one of the four faces. It has its own separate source.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Idi, said:
From Abaye's lecture I heard:
“You shall not make with Me”
means: You shall not make Me.
phrases.notes: Same letters, read with different vowels: אִתִּי ('with Me') becomes אוֹתִי ('Me').

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב הונא בריה דרב אידי מפירקיה דאביי שמיעא לי
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate source for the איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The human face is forbidden as part of the four-faces rule, which would contradict אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The human face is forbidden by a separate דרשה (לא תעשון אותי), so אביי's rule stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known איסור of making a full human face.

steps.title: Are images of the other heavenly attendants allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether images of the other attendants on high are permitted, and quotes a ברייתא that forbids images of all the angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really allowed to make images of the other attendants? A ברייתא teaches that 'Do not make with Me' means: do not make images of My attendants who serve Me on high, like אופנים, שרפים, חיות הקודש and מלאכי השרת!
steps.whatsHappening: Step 7 said only the four faces together and the human face are forbidden. Now the גמרא asks: does that mean all the other angels may be pictured? A ברייתא says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only specific images are forbidden, it would seem every other heavenly being is allowed. But this ברייתא lists a whole group of angels and forbids making images of all of them. So the 'only four faces' idea seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: Attendants, servants (here: beings that serve הקב"ה)
The holy 'living creatures', a type of angel

phrases.english: And are other attendants permitted?
phrases.notes: He means the other heavenly servants, besides the four faces and the human face from the last steps.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: 'You shall not make with Me',
do not make the likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me on high,
such as ofanim and seraphim
and the holy chayot and the ministering angels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר שַׁמָּשִׁין מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrow scope of the prohibition set up in steps 5 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only the four-faced image and the human face are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids images of all the angels on high, not just specific faces.

steps.title: Only attendants of the upper heaven are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the Torah forbade images only of the attendants in the highest heaven, meaning the angels, not the sun and moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Torah only forbade images of the attendants in the upper realm.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי accepts that all the angels are forbidden, but draws a line: only the beings of the upper heaven. That leaves the sun, moon and stars permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of limiting the ban to certain faces, אביי now limits it by location. Angels in the upper heaven are forbidden to picture; the lower heaven, where the sun and moon are, is not included. This keeps רבן גמליאל's moon pictures allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The upper realm, the highest heaven

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Torah forbade only
attendants that are in the upper realm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the prohibition to a specific category (by location).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only certain faces are forbidden, so the ברייתא forbidding all angels is a problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: All angels of the upper heaven are forbidden, but beings of the lower heaven, like the sun and moon, are not.

steps.title: Are the sun and moon really allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the beings of the lower heaven are permitted, quoting a ברייתא that includes sun, moon, stars and constellations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are the beings of the lower realm really allowed? A ברייתא teaches: 'that is in heaven' comes to include the sun, moon, stars and constellations; 'above' comes to include the ministering angels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's line. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the sun, moon and stars are included in the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the lower heaven is allowed. But this ברייתא reads the words 'in heaven' as including exactly those lower-heaven beings. So it looks like the sun and moon are forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower realm (the heaven of the sun, moon and stars)
To include (a word in the פסוק adds something)

phrases.english: And are those in the lower realm permitted?
But isn't it taught: 'that is in heaven'
phrases.notes: These words come from the second of the עשרת הדברות in שמות כ: no image of anything in heaven, on earth, or in the water.

phrases.english: comes to include sun and moon, stars and constellations,
'above' comes to include the ministering angels!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that lower-heaven beings may be pictured.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads 'in heaven' as including the sun, moon, stars and constellations.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about worshipping them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא from step 10 is talking about worshipping these things, not about just making their image.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about worshipping them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves אביי by saying the ברייתא is about a different איסור: serving them as gods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions: may you worship something, and may you make a picture of it. The ברייתא forbids worshipping the sun and moon, which is not what אביי was discussing. Making their image could still be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: When that ברייתא was taught (it was about...)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two איסורים here. Worshipping the sun is always forbidden; the question in this סוגיא is only whether you may make a picture of it.

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was about worshipping them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the ברייתא as dealing with a different איסור.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids making images of the sun and moon.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids worshipping them; making images of them may still be allowed.

steps.title: Then even a tiny worm should be included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the ברייתא is about worship, it should include even a tiny worm, since worshipping anything is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is about worshipping them, then even a tiny worm should be included too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 11. If the ברייתא is about worship, why list only big heavenly things?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worshipping anything at all is forbidden, even the smallest creature. So a ברייתא about worship should not need to list only grand things like the sun and stars. It should go all the way down to a tiny worm.

phrases.english: If it is about worshipping them,
then even a tiny worm too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְעׇבְדָם, אֲפִילּוּ שִׁלְשׁוּל קָטָן נָמֵי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about worship.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worship ban covers even the smallest creature, so the ברייתא's list of only heavenly bodies looks like it is about images, not worship.

steps.title: Yes, the same ברייתא does include a tiny worm
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees and shows that the rest of the same ברייתא does include mountains, seas and even a tiny worm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true, as it is taught: 'that is on the earth' includes mountains and hills, seas and rivers, streams and valleys; 'beneath' includes a tiny worm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא really does go all the way down to a tiny worm. This confirms the ברייתא is about worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The continuation of the same ברייתא reads 'on the earth' and 'beneath' to include mountains, rivers and even a tiny worm. That is exactly what step 12 said a ban on worship should include. So the whole ברייתא can be read as being about worship, which supports the answer of step 11.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so, as it is taught:
'that is on the earth' comes to include mountains and hills,
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק and the same ברייתא quoted in step 10.

phrases.english: seas and rivers, streams and valleys;
'beneath' comes to include a tiny worm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and supports step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge's point and shows the source already says it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists only heavenly bodies, so it must be about images.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא also includes earthly things and a tiny worm, so it is about worship.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids just making images of the sun and moon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether simply making images of the sun and moon is allowed, quoting a ברייתא that explicitly forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is just making them really allowed? A ברייתא teaches: 'Do not make with Me' means do not make the likeness of My attendants who serve before Me, such as the sun, moon, stars and constellations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that clearly talks about making images, and it names the sun and moon. This attacks אביי's answer of step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 and 13 avoided the earlier ברייתא by saying it was about worship. This ברייתא learns from 'Do not make with Me', which is about making, and it lists the sun, moon and stars. So even just making their image is forbidden, and אביי's upper/lower distinction falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Just making (an image), without worshipping it

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא separates two איסורים: worshipping something and just making its image. In the end, a ברייתא forbids even just making images of the sun, moon and stars, so אביי's answer does not hold, and the question about רבן גמליאל's pictures of the moon comes back. The next step gives a new answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source that making images of the sun, moon and stars is forbidden, even with no intent to worship them.

phrases.english: And is mere making permitted?
phrases.notes: He means just making a picture of the sun or moon, without any worship.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: 'You shall not make with Me',

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תַּעֲשׂוּן כִּדְמוּת שַׁמָּשַׁיי הַמְשַׁמְּשִׁין לְפָנַי,
phrases.english: do not make the likeness of My attendants who serve before Me,
such as sun and moon, stars and constellations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 11-13 explained the earlier ברייתא as about worship, this brings a new ברייתא that is clearly about making images.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim (step 9) that images of lower-heaven beings like the sun and moon are allowed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא based on 'Do not make with Me', a פסוק about making, explicitly forbids images of the sun, moon, stars and constellations.

steps.title: Others made the pictures for רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: רבן גמליאל was allowed to have the moon pictures because non-Jews made them for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל is different, because others made the pictures for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14 a new way. The rule is against a Jew making these images, and רבן גמליאל did not make his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 14 forbids making images of the sun and moon. This answer says the ban is on making them, not on owning them. Since non-Jews made רבן גמליאל's pictures, he did nothing wrong by keeping them.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel is different,
because others made them for him.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the pictures of the moon רבן גמליאל used when questioning witnesses.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ban to the act of making the image
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Owning an image of the moon is itself forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Only making it is forbidden. Owning one that others made is allowed.

steps.title: The case of רב יהודה's ring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: רב יהודה's seal was made by others, yet שמואל told him to ruin it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But others made a seal for רב יהודה, and שמואל still said to him: Sharp one, blind this one's eyes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15 using a real story. Even though others made רב יהודה's seal, שמואל did not let him keep it as it was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If owning an image made by others is fine, שמואל should not have objected. His order to deface the image suggests that owning it is also a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp one (שמואל's nickname for רב יהודה)
Blind its eyes, meaning deface the image

phrases.english: But there is Rav Yehuda,
for whom others made it,
phrases.notes: "It" is a seal ring carved with a human face.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, blind the eyes of this one!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that images made by others may be kept
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל made רב יהודה deface a seal that others made, so keeping such an image looks forbidden

steps.title: That ring had a raised image, so the problem was suspicion
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's seal had a raised image, and שמואל objected only because people might suspect him of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, his seal had a raised image, and the problem was suspicion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב יהודה's case was a special problem. The reason was not making an image but what people might think.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ring with a raised figure looks like something used for idol worship. שמואל objected to how it looked to others, so the answer about רבן גמליאל still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspicion that one serves עבודה זרה

phrases.english: There, his seal was raised,
and it was because of suspicion.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for שמואל's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל objected because owning any image is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: He objected only because a raised image on a worn ring causes suspicion

steps.title: A ברייתא about raised and sunken ring seals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports this: you may not wear a ring with a raised seal, but you may seal with it. For a sunken seal it is the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A ring with a raised seal may not be worn, but you may seal with it. A ring with a sunken seal may be worn, but you may not seal with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up the answer in step 17. Wearing a raised image is forbidden because of suspicion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing a raised figure looks like idol worship, so it is not allowed. Sealing with it is fine because the mark it leaves is sunken. A sunken seal is fine to wear, but sealing with it creates a raised image, which counts as making a forbidden image.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: A raised image on your ring is a problem of suspicion. Stamping out a raised image is a problem of making one.
steps.confusionAlert: The rules flip. A raised seal leaves a sunken mark, and a sunken seal leaves a raised mark.

phrases.english: As it is taught: A ring whose seal is raised,
it is forbidden to put it on,
but it is permitted to seal with it.
If its seal is sunken,
it is permitted to put it on,
but it is forbidden to seal with it.

steps.raayaObject: That a raised seal is forbidden to wear because of suspicion

steps.title: Great rabbis prayed in a שול with a statue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we really worry about suspicion, since רב, שמואל, שמואל's father and לוי prayed in a שול in נהרדעא that had a statue.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really worry about suspicion? But there was a שול in נהרדעא that had a statue, and רב, שמואל, שמואל's father and לוי went in and prayed there without worrying about suspicion!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from step 17 that suspicion is a real worry. Great rabbis prayed in a building with a statue and did not care what people might think.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying in front of a statue looks even more suspicious than wearing a ring. If these rabbis did not worry about it, why did שמואל worry about רב יהודה's ring?

keyTerms.meaning: Moved and settled (name of the שול)

phrases.english: And are we concerned about suspicion?
But there was that synagogue
that moved and settled in Neharde'a,
phrases.notes: This is what the שול was called. Its stones were brought over from ארץ ישראל and rebuilt there.

phrases.english: which had a statue in it,
and Rav and Shmuel would enter,
and Shmuel's father and Levi,
and pray there,
and they were not concerned about suspicion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: That suspicion is a reason to forbid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leading rabbis prayed near a statue without worrying about suspicion

steps.title: A crowd is different
steps.stepSummary: When many people are present, nobody suspects them of idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Many people are different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a group is not suspected. Only a person who is alone is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one thinks a whole congregation is secretly serving a statue. People assume the statue is just decoration. One person wearing a ring with a raised image can be suspected.

phrases.english: Many people are different.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a line between a group and one person
steps.terutzMaskana: Suspicion applies to one person, not to a crowd

steps.title: But רבן גמליאל was one person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבן גמליאל was one person, so his moon pictures should cause suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't רבן גמליאל one person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer from step 20 back on רבן גמליאל. If one person is suspected, his pictures should have been a problem too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said the pictures were allowed because others made them. Step 20 says one person can still be suspected. So רבן גמליאל, as one person with images, seems to have the same problem as רב יהודה.

phrases.english: But isn't Rabban Gamliel one person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 20 to רבן גמליאל
steps.kashyaTarget: The permission for רבן גמליאל's pictures
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One person is suspected, and רבן גמליאל was one person

steps.title: A נשיא is always surrounded by people
steps.stepSummary: Since רבן גמליאל was the נשיא, many people were always with him, so he counts like a group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he is the נשיא, many people are always found with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבן גמליאל was never really alone. As the leader, he always had a crowd around him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 20 protects a crowd from suspicion. A נשיא always has many people near him, so he falls under that rule.

phrases.english: Since he is the Nasi,
many people are always found with him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the case under the existing rule for groups
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל was a lone person who could be suspected
steps.terutzMaskana: A נשיא counts like a group, so there was no suspicion

steps.title: The pictures were made in pieces
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: רבן גמליאל's moon pictures were made of separate pieces, not one whole image.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: they were made in pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer step 21. The pictures were not complete images at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a complete image is forbidden. If the moon shapes were separate pieces that had to be put together, there was no full image to cause suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: If you want, say:
they were made in pieces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the קשיא of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the object so it is not a full image
steps.terutzMaskana: They were pieces, which are not forbidden

steps.title: רבן גמליאל made the pictures in order to learn
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: רבן גמליאל made the moon pictures to teach himself, and the פסוק only forbids learning idolatrous practices in order to do them, not in order to understand and teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: he made them to teach himself. The Torah says 'You shall not learn to do.' That means you may not learn in order to do, but you may learn in order to understand and to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer for why רבן גמליאל's moon pictures were allowed: he made them for learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two answers dealt with suspicion: he was always with many people, or the pictures were made of separate pieces. This answer is different. It says that even a forbidden image may be made when the purpose is learning. It reads 'לֹא תִּלְמַד לַעֲשׂוֹת' to mean that learning becomes forbidden only when it leads to doing, while learning 'to understand and to teach' is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: this introduces another possible answer
To teach oneself, or to learn
You shall not learn to do: the Torah's warning against copying the practices of other nations
To understand and to teach, or to give rulings

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא gave three answers for רבן גמליאל's moon pictures: (1) as the נשיא he always had many people with him, so nobody would suspect him; (2) the pictures were made of separate pieces; (3) he made them in order to learn, which is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer teaches a wider idea: something forbidden in order to do it may be allowed when it is done in order to learn, understand and teach.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
he made them to teach himself,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבן גמליאל, and "them" is the moon pictures from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: and it is written: "You shall not learn to do"
which means: but you may learn
in order to understand and to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, independent answer to the קשיא in step 21, alongside the answers in steps 22 and 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exemption based on purpose: making the image for learning is allowed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed that keeping moon pictures is forbidden no matter what the purpose is.
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition does not cover something made in order to learn, understand and teach, so רבן גמליאל was permitted.

steps.title: New משנה: two witnesses saw the moon in the morning in the east
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins with a story about two witnesses who testified that they saw the moon in the morning, in the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: It once happened that two people came and said: We saw it in the morning in the east.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here with a story about two witnesses. This line only sets up the story, and the rest of their testimony continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses say they saw the moon in the morning, in the east. Their full testimony and what the court did about it come right after this line. For now, just hold on to the details: two witnesses, morning, east.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
An incident, a story that actually happened

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a complete sentence. The משנה continues past this point, so do not try to decide yet what the ruling is.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There was an incident in which two people came
phrases.notes: The two are witnesses who came to testify about the new moon.

phrases.english: and they said: We saw it
in the morning in the east,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁבָּאוּ שְׁנַיִם וְאָמְרוּ: רְאִינוּהוּ שַׁחֲרִית בַּמִּזְרָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of רבן גמליאל's moon pictures ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only opens the story of two witnesses who say they saw the moon in the morning in the east.
